ABSTRACT Drought and salinity are two major factors limiting soybean productivity worldwide, and both stresses can negatively affect plant growth in similar manners by disrupting cellular redox homeostasis and metabolism. However, the regulatory networks coordinating transcriptional control and metabolic adaptation under both types of stress remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that the R2R3–MYB transcription factors GmMYB60a and GmMYB60b serve as core negative regulators of drought and salt tolerance in soybean.
